outOfScope: Global scheduler, role registry or organization workflow graph.
Exactly-once event transport or transactional outbox as a correctness prerequisite.
Deployment, AcceptanceSnapshot or Product QA semantics.
Execution-policy or strategy selection inside the activation boundary.
constraints: Event or queue delivery is not lifecycle, claim or execution authority.
Activation is not strategy selection and is not obligation creation.
Queue, cursor and local backoff state are disposable and reconstructable from canonical work state.
A stale queued hint cannot resurrect invalidated work.
Frontend and Backend independence is governed by exact semantic dependencies, not global development stages.
A durable runtime such as Restate may host activation mechanics but cannot become organizational source of truth or hidden scheduler.
invariants: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work
architectureDecisions: DOMAIN_ACTIVATION is a domain-local level-triggered reconciler over canonical actionable work, not a scheduler.
Wake-up events, watches, polls and restart scans are latency hints only; every reconcile re-reads canonical work, owning-domain and obligation/currentness state before claim.
Activation keys are exact projectId/workId/owningDomain identities. Role, stage, queue position and trigger payload never grant claim or execution authority.
Canonical domain scans are the recovery source. Queue/cursor/backoff state is disposable and may be lost without stranding persisted actionable work.
Duplicate hints converge through the existing organization claim/release fencing plus DomainExecutionController attempt currentness; activation adds no exactly-once transport requirement.
Activation never resolves ExecutionStrategy and never creates obligations. It hands one current released claim to the existing domain-execution HOW boundary.

BB-052 is a hard execution dependency. The worker must consume its DONE consolidated Living truth and current obligation/currentness APIs; if the delivered dependency contradicts these plan assumptions, execution returns to RESEARCH_SA rather than adapting silently.

After activation pre-check and claim/release, the exact source obligation/currentness observation is revalidated immediately before domain execution entry. Drift invalidates/fences the organization claim and the stale hint becomes NOOP.

Backend receives a domain-local strategy adapter over existing Backend worker/application primitives; createDurableBackendQaWorkflow is not reused as the strategy because QA cross-domain control is outside this boundary.
Frontend becomes a first-class independent domain with explicit contract/result/context/completion semantics and its own strategy descriptor; FE and BE have no implicit global stage barrier.
A domain outage affects only that domain's reconciliation/execution loop. Unrelated owning domains continue discovering and executing their own actionable work.
DomainActivationObservation is telemetry only and cannot become lifecycle, claim, obligation, strategy or publication authority.
implementationSlices: D1 — Activation [AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, INV-1..3]: implement exact DomainActivationKey, canonical scan and reconcile. Reconcile re-reads current work/owningDomain, returns NOOP for stale/wrong-domain work, never ranks work and never reads strategy policy.

D2 — Admission [AC-2..4, INV-1,4,5,8]: a domain-bound activation controller uses the existing claim/release authority, rechecks the exact BB-052 obligation/currentness after release, fences drift, then calls executeReleasedClaim({itemId,claimGeneration,receiptRef}) only.

D3 — Backend runtime [AC-5, AC-6, INV-4,7]: backend-execution-strategy implements the existing runtimeAdapter dispatch/recover contract over current Backend application/worker primitives. It emits Backend-owned outputs/evidence only; durable-backend-qa/composition is not the execution strategy.

D4 — Frontend runtime [AC-5, AC-6, INV-6,7]: frontend-contracts defines the exact FrontendWorkOrder/Context/Result in domainAutonomyContract.frontend; frontend-worker + frontend-application execute that contract; frontend-completion evaluates acceptanceRefs/evidence; frontend-execution-strategy maps dispatch/recover to the existing runtimeAdapter result. No Backend state is an input.

D5 — Domain composition + concurrency [AC-5..7, INV-6,7]: domain-runtime-composition creates separate BACKEND and FRONTEND activation/controller/runtimeAdapter instances sharing only canonical stores. fe-be-parallel.test uses two independent dispatch barriers and must observe both dispatches plus distinct policy/strategy/attempt/runtime invocation identities before either completes; one adapter failure cannot block the other.

D6 — Recovery/invalidation [AC-1,2,4,8, INV-2,8]: restart with no hints must rediscover canonical work; duplicate hints converge through claim/attempt currentness; obligation supersession before execution entry fences only that subject while unrelated domain work remains executable.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Persisted actionable work is rediscovered and processed after controller restart even when its original notification was lost.
evidenceRequired: Restart fixture drops the original hint, reconstructs from canonical scan, and enters one current claim/execution path.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Concurrent duplicate hints for one work item converge to one current claim/execution path.
evidenceRequired: Concurrent event+scan hints for the same exact work key produce one claim generation/current execution attempt; duplicates return NOOP/replay.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A wrong-domain activation attempt cannot claim or execute the work.
evidenceRequired: Wrong-domain controller/principal is rejected before executable claim or DomainExecutionController entry.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Obligation supersession between activation pre-check and execution entry prevents execution through the post-release currentness recheck.
evidenceRequired: Race fixture supersedes the exact source obligation after pre-check; post-release recheck fences the claim and no execution dispatch occurs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Frontend and Backend work can progress concurrently and independently under their own domain execution strategies.
evidenceRequired: frontend-domain proves FrontendWorkOrder is derived only from the bound OrganizationWorkContract; FrontendContext resolves exact requiredArtifactRefs; Frontend completion consumes acceptanceRefs/evidence and no Backend state.

fe-be-parallel starts unrelated BACKEND and FRONTEND reconciles together and observes both dispatchStarted before either barrier release, with distinct policyRef, strategyRef, attemptId and runtimeInvocationKey.
No activation input contains strategyRef/runtime-adapter choice and no cross-domain stage/next-role state gates either domain.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An outage in one domain leaves unrelated work in another domain actionable and able to progress.
evidenceRequired: With both domains independently actionable, inject a dispatch/recovery failure into one domain runtime and prove the unrelated domain still discovers, claims, dispatches and reaches its own current completion path.
The failed domain's attempt/claim state is not used as a prerequisite or lock by the progressing domain.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Removing a manual next-role dispatcher does not stop progress for persisted actionable work.
evidenceRequired: Fixture has no manual next-role dispatcher and still progresses persisted actionable FE/BE work from canonical reconciliation.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Partial upstream invalidation suppresses only affected activation subjects while unrelated domain work remains actionable.
evidenceRequired: Partial invalidation makes only affected activation subjects NOOP/fenced while unrelated work remains actionable and executes.
Negative case proves trigger/event payload fields cannot authorize claim, execution or publication.
Lost/deleted hint queue state followed by restart scan yields the same actionable work; queue/cursor deletion changes no canonical truth.
Activation API accepts exact work identities and exposes no role/stage ranking or next-work selection path.
Activation cannot supply/resolve an ExecutionStrategy; existing DomainExecutionController policy/strategy authority remains required.
Activation cannot create or mutate CrossDomainObligation; only current BB-052 obligation state may be consumed.
FE work is not blocked by unrelated Backend stage state; only explicit semantic dependencies affect actionability.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
evidenceRequired: One-domain-down test proves unrelated domain progress continues.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work
evidenceRequired: Stale queued hint after selective invalidation cannot resurrect, claim or execute invalidated work.

invariantCoverage.invariant: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work

negativeVerificationCases: An event payload that contains principal/domain/strategy fields cannot directly authorize claim, execution or publication.
A request to activate a BACKEND/FRONTEND role or workflow stage without an exact projectId/workId/owningDomain key is rejected.
A controller configured for the wrong owning domain cannot claim or execute the work.
Deleting or losing queue/cursor/hint state cannot strand canonical actionable work; restart scan rediscovers it.
Concurrent duplicate event and scan hints cannot create two current claim generations or two current execution attempts for one work item.
Activation cannot resolve, choose or override ExecutionStrategy; existing execution-policy authority remains mandatory.
Activation cannot create a CrossDomainObligation or make a non-current obligation current.
Frontend cannot be forced to wait for a whole Backend stage when its exact semantic dependencies are satisfied.
A stale queued hint after obligation/selective invalidation becomes NOOP/fenced and cannot resurrect executable capability.
A Backend activation outage cannot prevent unrelated Frontend work from being discovered and executed.
FrontendWorkOrder/context/completion that reads Backend stage/session/completion state is rejected; only the bound Frontend WorkContract and its exact semantic dependencies may gate Frontend.
A parallel fixture that starts one domain only after the other completes is rejected even if both eventually succeed.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: Persisted actionable work is rediscovered and processed after controller restart even when its original notification was lost.
Concurrent duplicate hints for one work item converge to one current claim/execution path.
A wrong-domain activation attempt cannot claim or execute the work.
Obligation supersession between activation pre-check and execution entry prevents execution through the post-release currentness recheck.
Frontend and Backend work can progress concurrently and independently under their own domain execution strategies.
objectiveCoverage.coverageArgument: D3 binds the current Backend primitives to one domain runtime. D4 defines a complete Frontend order/context/result/completion/recovery contract and its own runtime adapter. D5 composes separate controllers and proves actual dispatch overlap with distinct policy/strategy/attempt/runtime identities before either domain completes.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: An outage in one domain leaves unrelated work in another domain actionable and able to progress.
Removing a manual next-role dispatcher does not stop progress for persisted actionable work.
Partial upstream invalidation suppresses only affected activation subjects while unrelated domain work remains actionable.

laneContracts.input: BB-053 OBJECTIVE plus current delivered BB-048 Living truth and BB-052 READY dependency contract at exact researchBaselineSha
laneContracts.binding: objective ref/hash plus exact researchBaselineSha source evidence
laneContracts.convergence: all researchGaps are closed and Jev returns SATISFIED for every objective/readiness claim
forbidden: treat unfinished BB-052 source as delivered truth

laneContracts.input: exact READY_IMPLEMENT_PLAN ref/content hash plus DONE BB-052 consolidated Living truth
laneContracts.binding: plan hash, exact candidate SHA/tree, criterion-specific verification logs and Jev candidate judgment
laneContracts.convergence: every acceptance/invariant criterion plus Living Docs is SATISFIED and exact evaluated candidate is preserved in main

verificationScopeNote: BB-053 uses criterion-specific activation/recovery/parallelism/invalidation checks plus existing organization/domain-execution regressions and the full agentic regression suite. Workspace-wide npm run verify remains repository CI, not semantic evidence for an individual Integration D criterion.

livingDocs.statement: The delivered Integration D Living Docs accurately describe domain-local level-triggered activation, claim/execution admission, FE/BE independent domain strategies, recovery and non-authoritative wake-up hints.

domainAutonomyContract.workIdentity: Both domains consume immutable OrganizationWorkContract subjects. owningDomain + workloadType select the existing execution-policy subject; workContractRef + itemId select the existing execution-attempt subject. No role/stage state participates.

runtimes.activation: one BACKEND-bound DomainActivationController + trusted BACKEND principal
runtimes.execution: one createDomainExecutionController instance bound to backend-execution-strategy runtimeAdapter
runtimes.strategyAuthority: executionPolicySubjectKey(contract.owningDomain, contract.workloadType) resolves the BACKEND strategyRef; activation cannot provide it
runtimes.application: adapter dispatch/recover maps the bound WorkContract to existing Backend prepare/run/recover primitives and returns only Backend-owned outputs/evidence

runtimes.activation: one FRONTEND-bound DomainActivationController + trusted FRONTEND principal
runtimes.execution: one createDomainExecutionController instance bound to frontend-execution-strategy runtimeAdapter
runtimes.strategyAuthority: executionPolicySubjectKey(contract.owningDomain, contract.workloadType) resolves the FRONTEND strategyRef; activation cannot provide it
runtimes.application: adapter dispatch/recover maps the bound WorkContract to the explicit Frontend contract below and returns only Frontend-owned outputs/evidence

frontend.order: FrontendWorkOrder {workContractRef, projectId, itemId, summary, requiredArtifactRefs, expectedArtifactKind, expectedOutputRefs, acceptanceRefs}; derived only from the bound OrganizationWorkContract.
frontend.context: FrontendContext {workContractRef, inputs[]} resolves exactly requiredArtifactRefs through an injected artifact reader; it contains no Backend session/completion/stage field.
frontend.result: FrontendWorkResult {status: APPLIED|BLOCKED|FAILED, outputArtifactRefs, verificationCandidateRefs, counterevidenceRefs, effectRefs, traceRefs, proposedDerivationEdges}; frontend-execution-strategy converts it to the existing runtimeAdapter result shape.
frontend.completion: frontend-completion.js evaluates the WorkContract acceptanceRefs against Frontend result evidence and produces the domain completion input; no Backend decision is an input.
frontend.recovery: recover is keyed by the same executionAttempt binding/runtimeInvocationKey and Frontend workContractRef; it cannot remap work or inspect Backend progress.

parallelism.precondition: Use one unrelated BACKEND work contract and one unrelated FRONTEND work contract with no dependency edge; publish distinct ACTIVE policies and strategy descriptors.
parallelism.proof: Promise.all starts both reconciles. Each runtime adapter emits dispatchStarted then waits on its own deferred barrier. Before releasing either barrier assert both dispatchStarted plus distinct workContractRef, executionPolicyRef, executionStrategyRef, executionAttemptId and runtimeInvocationKey.
parallelism.isolation: Reject one domain adapter/barrier and prove the other still discovers, claims, dispatches and reaches its own current completion path.
